_readme: An entry here is NOT an exemption and NOT a suppression. It records a site that
matches the detector's shape — a company derived from the authenticated principal
with no membership-validity condition — but where source inspection established
the derived company does not authorize anything. Each entry must name what the
value IS used for, and what would have to change for it to become a defect.
Adding an entry to silence a site that DOES authorize is the failure this file
exists to make visible. Fix such a site instead: add the status predicate, filter
in code, or route through an approved tenant primitive.
Entries are keyed by file:line and go stale when code moves. The guard reports
stale keys so they are removed rather than left to rot into blanket cover.

accepted.reason: The derived company is written to access_requests.organization_id on the requester's own PENDING row. It is never used as a tenant predicate for a read or a write, and it grants nothing: the row is a REQUEST for access, and approval is a separate super-admin flow that establishes access on its own terms.
accepted.caveat: The field does influence which organisation an approver sees the request under, so a caller holding only a stale membership would have their request attributed to that organisation. That is a routing and disclosure question about a self-submitted request, not an authorization decision, and it does not confer access.
accepted.would_become_a_defect_if: access_requests.organization_id is ever read back as the tenant for a subsequent read, write or approval decision without re-establishing membership.
accepted.reverified: 2026-09-13 against main 07acd0a7: same line, same shape. Every reader of access_requests.organization_id (admin/access-requests/approve, onboarding/complete, onboarding/setup-company, admin/external-users) filters status='approved', and the only approval path (admin/access-requests/approve) overwrites organization_id with the admin-chosen company, so the requester-derived value is never read back as a tenant.
accepted.moved: 2026-09-15 STEP 3AH-91 integration: 108 → 110. SEC91-W2E added one import and one comment line above it (trusted client IP); the membership query is byte-identical and none of the readers listed above changed.

accepted.reason: assignSuperAdmin falls back to the target user's most recent membership row (any status) only to choose WHICH company the SUPER_ADMIN membership row is bound to, when the caller gave no organizationId and the user has no active_company_id. It authorizes nothing: the grant itself is authorized by requireCapability(identity.admin.assign) + step-up in every mode before assignSuperAdmin runs.
accepted.caveat: A stale (inactive / invited / expired) membership can be chosen as the binding company. With the Closure-015L/015M database guard (supabase/proposals/closure015l/01_*, 02_*) a binding company that is missing, disabled, suspended or soft-deleted is refused by the trigger and by assign_super_admin.
accepted.would_become_a_defect_if: the derived company is ever used as a tenant predicate or to grant anything other than the governed SUPER_ADMIN binding, or the identity.admin.assign + step-up gate in front of assignSuperAdmin is removed.
accepted.note: Previously classified SAFE only because the existing-row branch (row.status === 'active') fell inside the detector's 1600-character context window; Closure-015M inserted the governed assign_super_admin call between them, which moved it out of the window. The query itself is byte-identical (line 467 → 468 by one added import).
